title: Stand a folded birthday card on a shelf as a tent: turn it crease-up by its front leaf and set both edges down open
instruction: Stand the birthday card up on the shelf where it lies, open like a tent with its crease on top and its picture facing you, and let go of it.
context: Standing a birthday card up on a shelf is something almost everyone does. A folded card is two light leaves joined at a springy crease. Lying closed it gapes a little at the front, so it can only be taken by its front leaf, and only at its edges: the leaves are 0.36 mm card. To stand it, it must be turned crease-up, which leaves the back leaf hanging loose from the crease, and set down on both thin bottom edges, the back edge first and then the crease carried over it until the front edge lands, so the card ends open and steady with the crease over the spot. Let go of it while it is still being turned and the 13.5 g card falls back flat; set down too closed or too open, the crease pushes or pulls it until friction under its edges holds it (between about 36 and 83 degrees here). Unlike standing a tablet on its fold-out support or a picture frame on a ledge, there is no stand, stop or detent: just two loose leaves and a crease.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the desk (the table top). Shelf: a short oak-effect melamine desk shelf (melamine-faced wood chipboard), an 18 mm board 220 along y by 220 along x whose top is 120 above the desk, standing on an 18 mm back panel under its back edge; its front edge at x = 175, centred on y = 0. A 12 mm blue sticker dot is on it at (285, 0). Card: a Nitelemn white 5 x 7 in folded tent card (110 lb / 300 g/m2 coated paper cover stock, a 10 x 7 in sheet scored and folded to 5 x 7 in; Amazon B0GQXMQW8J), 13.5 g, two leaves each 127 (crease to free edge) by 178 (along the crease), about 0.36 thick (estimate). Its front leaf is printed with five balloons (red, yellow, blue, green, purple) above a red HAPPY BIRTHDAY banner, the balloons toward the crease. It lies closed on the shelf, picture up, the crease along y on the far side (x = 348.5), the free edges toward the robot (x = 221.5), and the middle of its 127 x 178 outline over the dot. Lying closed, the crease holds the front leaf 11.8 degrees open, its free edge 26 above the back leaf. Crease (estimates; no maker figure): a spring toward 45 degrees open, 0.0071 N m per radian, damping 0.0003 N m s per radian. Card on melamine friction 0.30 (estimate). Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. The README lists every collider and mass.
scoring: Judged 10 s after both hands have let go, with a ruler, a protractor and a photo from above. Let go: both grippers' centre points at least 10 cm from the card. Standing: the card rests on the shelf on its two free (bottom) edges, each within 4 mm of the shelf's top at both ends, the crease at least 40 mm above both, and nothing else touches the shelf. It must have stood, let go and still (over each second, the crease's middle and the free edges' corners moved under 1 mm) for the whole 10 s. Opening: the angle between the leaves at the crease. Facing: the direction the picture side faces, seen from above. 1.0: standing, open 30 to 90 degrees, the picture facing the robot (-x) within 20 degrees, the crease's middle within 40 mm of the dot. 0.6: standing, open 20 to 120 degrees, any facing, the crease's middle within 80 mm of the dot. 0.3: standing on the shelf crease-up, outside those limits. 0: anything else: lying, on its side or face, crease down, off the shelf, still held or touched, moving, or (real trials) creased anywhere but its fold: a new crease is a visible fold line, or a bend that stays over 10 degrees when that leaf is laid flat on the shelf. Possible scores: 0, 0.3, 0.6, 1.0.
reset_notes: Close the card, lay it on its mark (middle over the dot, crease along y away from the robot, picture up; within 1 cm and 5 degrees) and leave it 30 s so the crease settles to its lying gape. Use a new card from the pack when the lying gape falls under 8 degrees or the card is marked or bent. Zero object jitter.
fidelity: The card is two rigid leaves (true size and mass) on a hinge with a spring and damper for the crease; the spring's rest angle and stiffness are estimates set so the card lies open 11.8 degrees. Real leaves bend a little; these do not, so no new crease can form in simulation. Each leaf's collider is 1.0 mm thick (real 0.36 mm) for stable pad and edge contacts. The picture is thin coloured patches. Card-on-melamine friction is an estimate.
